findings.behavior: MIME extended parameters can override the actual charset, allowing a disallowed charset through. Preserve the literal charset parameter when checking the policy.
findings.evidence: Reproduced through ContentCharset("utf-8") with a nonempty POST body: Content-Type `text/plain; charset=latin-1; charset*=UTF-8''utf-8` returns 415 in baseline and 200 in candidate. The continuation form `charset=latin-1; charset*0=utf-; charset*1=8` also changes from 415 to 200. Conversely, `charset=utf-8; charset*=UTF-8''latin-1` changes from 200 to 415. mime.ParseMediaType folds these extended parameters into params["charset"], violating the requirement to preserve disallowed-charset behavior.

findings.behavior: A stray quote inside a malformed unquoted parameter hides subsequent charset parameters, breaking legacy compatibility and potentially accepting a disallowed charset.
findings.evidence: Public HTTP probes with a nonempty body demonstrated that Content-Type: text/plain; note=foo"bar; charset=utf-8 returns 204 in baseline but 415 in candidate with ContentCharset("UTF-8"). With charset=latin-1 and ContentCharset("UTF-8", ""), baseline returns 415 but candidate returns 204. The fallback toggles quoted mode at the embedded quote, skips the real charset, and treats it as absent. Recognize quoted parameter values without letting stray quotes in malformed unquoted values hide later parameters.
